name: Real or scripted event flag
plain: Every click and key event says whether the browser made it or a script made it.
meaning: Event.isTrusted is true for events created by the browser from real input and false for events a page script creates with dispatchEvent or element.click(). Agents that drive the browser through the DevTools Protocol send input the browser treats as real, so they pass. Agents that script clicks inside the page fail.

steps: Page listens for click, key and pointer events
False values from user actions suggest scripts

fields.name: isTrusted
fields.range: true when the browser created the event

limits.headline: Can tell if a click came from a real input path or from page script
limits.user_action: Nothing. It is on every event
can: Check the flag on click, key and pointer events
Spot in page scripts that fake clicks
Combine with timing and movement data
cannot: Catch agents that send real input through the DevTools Protocol
Tell a person from a remote controlled browser
Block browser extensions that act for you
limits.differs: Tools that send input through the browser's own input path produce trusted events, so the flag only catches simple scripts.

story.what_it_is: The browser stamps each event as genuine or generated by a script, and the page can read the stamp.

marketing.name: Event.isTrusted
marketing.pitch: Docs say the property is true when the event was generated by a user action.

story.for_you: You never see it. Your own clicks are trusted. Browser extensions and macro tools that fake clicks in the page can be ignored by sites.
story.for_makers: A false value is a strong sign of an in page script. A true value proves little, because DevTools Protocol input is trusted. Do not rely on it for security decisions alone.

use_cases.example: A bank page ignores untrusted clicks on the transfer button.
A checkout button refuses untrusted click events to stop in page bots.
An ad unit only counts clicks whose event is trusted.
A browser game drops untrusted key events from auto play scripts.
A tester finds that element.click() fails a site that wants real input.
A site must still accept assistive tools that send trusted input.

technical_bounds: Some browser features require trusted events anyway

abuse: Blocking legitimate assistive or automation tools
